questions.text:
Procedures P1 and P2 have a producer-consumer relationship, communicating by the use of a set of shared buffers.

P1 :
repeat
Obtain an empty buffer
Fill it
Return a full buffer
forever

P2:
repeat
Obtain a full buffer
Empty it
Return an empty buffer
forever

Increasing the number of buffers is likely to do which of the following?

I. Increase the rate at which requests are satisfied (throughput)
II. Decrease the likelihood of deadlock
III. Increase the ease of achieving a correct implementation
questions.solution:
More buffers let the producer run further ahead of the consumer, smoothing out speed differences, so throughput can increase. They do not affect deadlock or make a correct implementation easier.

Answer: I only

questions.text: The Operating System of a computer may periodically collect all the free memory space to form contiguous block of free space. This is called:
questions.solution:
The keyed answer is garbage collection: reclaiming free memory and gathering it together (by compacting allocated blocks) into one contiguous free block.

Answer: Garbage Collection

questions.text: Disk requests come to a disk driver for cylinders in the order 10, 22, 20, 2, 40, 6 and 38 at a time when the disk drive is reading from cylinder 20. The seek time is 6 ms/cylinder. The total seek time, if the disk arm scheduling algorithms is first-come-first-served is
questions.solution:
FCFS from 20: 10 (10), 22 (12), 20 (2), 2 (18), 40 (38), 6 (34), 38 (32) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 146 cylinders.
Seek time = 146 [latex]\times[/latex] 6 = 876 ms, which is not among the options.

Answer: None of the above

questions.text:
A computer has 1000K of main memory. The jobs arrive and finish in the following sequence.
Job 1 requiring 200 K arrives
Job 2 requiring 350 K arrives
Job 3 requiring 300 K arrives
Job 1 finishes
Job 4 requiring 120 K arrives
Job 5 requiring 150 K arrives
Job 6 requiring 80 K arrives
Among best fit and first fit, which performs better for this sequence?
questions.solution:
After jobs 1-3: used 0-850; job 1 finishes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] holes of 200K (start) and 150K (end).
- First fit: job 4 (120) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 200 hole (80 left); job 5 (150) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 150 hole; job 6 (80) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] the 80 hole True all fit.
- Best fit: job 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 150 hole (30 left); job 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 200 hole (50 left); job 6 (80) fits nowhere False.

Answer: First fit

questions.text: Consider a system having m resources of the same type. These resources are shared by 3 processes A,B,C, which have peak time demands of 3,4,6 respectively. The minimum value of m that ensures that deadlock will never occur is:
questions.solution:
Worst case: every process holds one less than its peak: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 units. One more unit lets some process finish, so deadlock is impossible.

m = 10 + 1 = 11

Answer: 11
